what_this_is: Who every Trillion email comes from and how it looks, the one row src/mail-sender.mjs reads for every email the app sends (space invitations, sign-in codes, notices, community digests, the emails that follow a sign-up) and that gettrillion.ai's email list reads too (dev/trillion-site worker/mail.js). `send_binding` is the Worker's Cloudflare Email Sending binding (the deploy binds this name; gettrillion.ai is onboarded for sending). `from` is the sender on every email; a row that sends may give only its own `reply_to` (a community owner's address). `postal_address` is the physical mailing address US law (CAN-SPAM) requires in every marketing email (the support address on Trillion's own Stripe account, acct_1UK4SGFVD6SXIxQu). `brand` is the mark at the top of every email, and `palette_roles` names, for each colour role the shared email part (parts/ui/show/document-page emailMessageHtml) reads, the workspace look's variable it comes from (src/page-look.mjs); a see-through colour is laid over `paper` so every email client shows it solid. `font_roles` names, the same way, the look's faces the email is set in (text, titles and quotes, code), so an email never names a face of its own. `provider` names this way of sending in the record every sent email leaves (src/sent.mjs, the `provider` of a `sent` record). `written_email_copies` says who gets a BCC copy of every written email (tool:send-an-email, src/mail-sender.mjs sendWrittenEmail): `account_owner` is the sending account's own address, so each one lands in the owner's own mail and its Sent record opens in their inbox.

refused_before_dispatch_codes._what: The codes the sending binding gives for a send it refused before dispatch (the provider's documented codes for a send it refused, https://developers.cloudflare.com/email-service/api/send-emails/workers-api/). A send that throws with any other code, or none, may have gone out, so src/mail-sender.mjs deliver answers it unknown: true and it is not sent again blindly.

senders._what: Who a written email (tool:send-an-email) comes from when it is sent for one account. A row names the account's own address (`owner`, the address its copy goes to) and the Trillion address and name its mail goes out from (`from`, an address on a domain this account's sending binding is onboarded for). An account with no row sends from `from` above, so mail for anyone defaults to a Trillion address and a non-Trillion sender needs its own row. Read by src/mail-sender.mjs senderFor.

per_person._what: How many emails one address may be sent, counted from the sent log below (src/mail-sender.mjs sendMail). Each limit covers the kinds it names (`kinds`) or every kind but those it names (`all_kinds_except`); a send that would make more than `most` of those within `window_minutes` is not sent, and the sender gets `says`. A sending row names its kind; one that names none is `default_kind`. Set on 2026-09-30, after a paying customer was sent about 30 emails in one day. Notices about who may confirm changes (kind account-authority, src/passkey-authority.json) have their own allowance, as many as that file lets be told, so other mail can never use up the room they are told in.

limits.says: Four sign-in codes were already sent to this email in the last hour. Use the newest one, or wait a little before asking again.
Four codes to open shared things were already sent to this email in the last hour. Use the newest one, or wait a little before asking again.
Three notices about who may confirm changes on this account were already sent to this email today.
This person was already sent three emails from Trillion today, so this one was not sent.

sent_log._what: Every email sent, written under the APP_KV key `key_prefix` + the BLAKE3 identity of the lowercased address, as [{ at, kind, subject }], kept `days`. A kind in `subject_kept_out_for` is written without its subject, since a sign-in code's subject carries the code.

held_for_proofs._what: An email to a proof account's own address (any pattern of src/proof-account-names.json) is never handed to the sending binding, so live proofs never spend the account's daily sending quota (on 2026-10-03, 136 of the day's sends were proof checkouts' purchase emails). One to a `handed_on` proof inbox (src/inbound-mail-settings.json) is handed straight to that inbox's keeper, as the round trip would have handed it; any other is written in the sent log and answered as kept. `kept_in_inbox` and `not_kept` are what the answer's kept_for_proof says.
held_for_proofs.kept_in_inbox: kept in the proof inbox without sending
held_for_proofs.not_kept: a proof address, so not sent

daily._what: How many emails this account's sending binding takes in a day (UTC), counted under APP_KV `key_prefix` + the day. Cloudflare caps the account's sends per day (`most`, read from the dashboard on 2026-10-04: 200); once only `keep_back` remain, only the kinds in `kept_for` still go, so a sign-in code, and a notice about who may confirm changes on an account, always has room. A send the binding refuses with `provider_full_code` fills the day.
daily.says: Trillion has nearly reached today's email limit and keeps what is left for sign-in codes, so this email was not sent.
